## From public files to defensible research data

The pipeline makes the decisions between download and analysis visible,
testable, and reviewable. Each layer answers a different reproducibility
question.
:::

::: {.workflow-grid}
::: {.workflow-card .card-blue}
<span class="step-number">01</span>

### Acquire

Retrieve declared files directly from official CDC/NCHS sources using a
reviewed, version-controlled catalog.
:::

::: {.workflow-card .card-cyan}
<span class="step-number">02</span>

### Validate

Stop early when source dimensions, schemas, participant keys, or merge
contracts do not match expectations.
:::

::: {.workflow-card .card-teal}
<span class="step-number">03</span>

### Harmonize

Keep component-specific scientific rules separate from generic acquisition so
important survey distinctions remain explicit.
:::

::: {.workflow-card .card-coral}
<span class="step-number">04</span>

### Document

Record retrieval times, source URLs, file hashes, dimensions, validation
results, and release versions for later review.
:::
:::

::: {.site-section}
::: {.feature-layout}
::: {.feature-copy}
<p class="eyebrow eyebrow-dark">Protection by design</p>

## Scientific meaning is part of the pipeline

The 2001–2002 second CBC examination is a convenience sample without survey
weights. This project preserves those repeat observations separately instead
of silently appending them to the representative primary examination data.

That safeguard prevents **557 duplicate participants** from entering the
combined CBC-demographic output unnoticed.

[Read the scientific rationale](NhanesDownloadScripts.qmd#cbc-first-and-second-examinations){.text-link}
:::

::: {.feature-panel}
<p class="panel-kicker">What the checks protect</p>

- Source availability and expected row counts
- Participant-key uniqueness by cycle
- Record-level and merge-granularity contracts
- Primary versus repeat examination roles
- Reproducible provenance and output validation
:::
:::
:::

::: {.site-section}
<p class="eyebrow eyebrow-dark">Designed to expand</p>

## A foundation for more NHANES components

::: {.principle-grid}
::: {.principle-card}
### Manifest-driven

New source files begin as reviewed catalog entries—not URLs buried inside
analysis notebooks.
:::

::: {.principle-card}
### Component-aware

Each component receives its own granularity, harmonization, eligibility, and
weighting review.
:::

::: {.principle-card}
### Citation-ready

Versioned releases, provenance hashes, and explicit source documentation make
reuse easier to describe and audit.
:::
:::
